paper_title: Thermal stress and antioxidant enzyme activity in Parthenium beetles (biologically impossible repeated per-larva enzyme values)
paper_authors: Physiological Entomology (2025); DOI 10.1111/phen.12475. PubPeer-reported value-substitution / sample-count inconsistency (Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.4mw6m90mp).

experimental_data.note: Dryad deposit. Sheet 'DATA': 350 rows, each nominally one independent larva, columns Duration/Setup/Stage/SOD(D)/CAT(E)/LPO(F). PubPeer reports biologically impossible repeated values: e.g. SOD is identical to 15 sig figs between different larvae in the same treatment group, and CAT values repeat with a single altered digit.

claims.claim_atom: In the raw data (Experimental_Data.xlsx, sheet 'DATA'), each of the 350 rows is presented as one independent larva, and the paper's ANOVA uses df that imply ~350 independent samples. Yet the SOD activity for the larva in row 61 (Cold/Second) is D61=0.21938013442867818, byte-identical to 15 significant figures to the larva in row 55 (also Cold/Second, D55=0.21938013442867818). An enzyme assay on two independently prepared larval homogenates cannot return a value equal to machine precision. This is not an isolated coincidence: across the 350 rows only 311 of the SOD values, 301 of the CAT values, and 291 of the LPO values are unique, and the repeats do not co-occur row-wise (a given row matches different rows in SOD, CAT and LPO), which rules out honest whole-row duplication and points to per-cell value substitution. PubPeer additionally documents CAT values repeated with a single altered digit (e.g. 140.49263461576285 at rows 52/54/56/57/59 vs 130.492634615763 at row 61). This anomaly is out of scope for the file-internal COLUMN detectors: (1) the duplicate-column detector compares whole columns for byte-identity or offset — no whole column is a duplicate here; the repeats are scattered WITHIN each column at different rows; (2) fixed-offset / paired-ratio detectors look for column-to-column arithmetic relations — none exists; (3) the claim loci are single cells (D61, D55), which the relationship verifier treats as too-short-to-relate and returns 'independent'. Detecting it requires the biological fact that independent per-larva assays cannot coincide to 15 sig figs, plus a within-column uniqueness/sample-count audit against the stated df — not a column relationship.
claims._adjudication: inconsistent: 各行が独立した幼虫 1 個体を表すはずだが、row61(Cold/Second)の SOD D61=0.21938013442867818 が row55(同 Cold/Second)の D55 と 15 桁完全一致。独立に調製した幼虫ホモジネートの酵素アッセイが機械精度で一致することは生物学的に不可能。350 行中 SOD ユニーク値は 311、CAT 301、LPO 291 のみで、重複は行単位で揃わない(行ごとに SOD/CAT/LPO が別々の行と一致)→ 正直な行複製ではなくセル単位の値置換。CAT は 1 桁改変の反復も存在(140.4926→130.4926)。B3 検出器は列間関係を探すが、これは列内の散在行の反復であり、単一セル(D61/D55)は短すぎて independent 判定→no_flag。発見には『独立個体アッセイは 15 桁一致しない』生物学的事実+列内ユニーク性/サンプル数監査が必要。

claims.claim_atom: The SOD activity for the larva in row 2 (Control/Second) is D2=0.2286045627376426, a value that is unique across all 350 rows of the DATA sheet — it is not shared with any other larva. This is exactly what a genuine independent per-larva measurement should look like: high-precision floating-point assay output with no exact partner elsewhere in the column. Its uniqueness is consistent with an honest measurement.
claims._adjudication: consistent(clean): row2(Control/Second)の SOD D2=0.2286045627376426 は 350 行中で一意=他のどの幼虫とも共有しない。真の独立個体測定が持つべき性質(高精度浮動小数点で列内に完全一致相手なし)と整合。clean claim。

claims.claim_atom: The CAT (catalase) activity for the larva in row 3 (Control/Second) is E3=121.97297719571615, a value unique across all 350 rows. Unlike the CAT values at rows 52/54/56/57/59 (all exactly 140.49263461576285) and the single-digit-altered 130.492634615763 at row 61 that PubPeer flags, this measurement has no exact or near-exact partner in the column and is consistent with a genuine independent catalase assay.

metadata._lane: Detector-disjoint holdout case (value_substitution + sample_count_mismatch / #4;#7). Anomaly = per-cell values copy-pasted between different larvae WITHIN a column (some with a single altered digit), so the stated per-larva sample count exceeds the true number of independent observations. Out-of-family: not a duplicate column, constant offset, paired ratio, or cross-sheet copy; single-cell claim loci fall under the len<2 verifier guard. Requires the biological fact that independent assays cannot coincide to 15 sig figs + a within-column uniqueness audit.
metadata._grounding_summary: openpyxl-parsed the DATA sheet locally (350 rows). Verified PubPeer claims: D61==D55=0.21938013442867818; E52=E54=E56=E57=E59=140.49263461576285, E61=130.492634615763; F61==F56=0.23014401517764746. Unique-value counts: SOD 311/350, CAT 301/350, LPO 291/350 — repeats scattered within columns, not aligned row-wise. Clean anchors D2 and E3 are unique across all 350 rows.
metadata._detector_note: value_substitution / sample_count_mismatch is outside the B3 detector family (duplicate-column / fixed-offset / paired-ratio / cross-sheet-reuse). The repeats are WITHIN a column at scattered rows (not a column-to-column relation), and all claim loci are single cells that the relationship verifier scores as 'independent' (length < 2). Expected B3: no_flag on all claims. NOTE: a naive pairwise row scan WOULD find the exact SOD/LPO repeats, but the B3 node-forensics detector operates on the adapter-fed src/tgt series per claim, where single cells never fire — this is precisely why the anomaly is disjoint from the deployed detector.
